Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: model-fit & structured-output eval plan (next steps)

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. This thread captures the simplest path to answer the two questions you called out: 1) model fit for your clinical summarization use-case, and 2) reliable structured output (JSON schema) for downstream analytics.

Recap / what we heard
- Use-case: ingest multi-section visit notes -> extract diagnoses, active medications, and a short clinician summary (free text + structured JSON).
- Volume: ~15k notes/month today; peak bursts up to 1.2k/day.
- Quality bar: >95% field-level extraction precision on med list and diagnoses; summary must be clinically accurate (low hallucination).
- Compliance: must run inside VPC (Private deployment) or Dedicated with SOC2 evidence; PHI handling constraints noted.

Proposed next steps (recommended, minimal friction):
1) Shared eval run (2 week): Redwood runs a structured-output eval on a 500-note sample you provide (anonymized) against the prompt_set_v1.json attached. We’ll evaluate model candidates and return token-level latency and field-level precision/recall.
2) Model candidates to benchmark (initial): open-llama-3-13b-instruct, redwood-instruct-7b-quant, and a larger candidate redwood-14b-flan-style (if you want higher recall). We’ll include a quantized variant to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
3) Tooling / function call testing: we’ll exercise function-calling paths with a JSON schema (attached) and a retry/backoff config. We’ll surface any schema mismatches and provide a remediation checklist (example: stable field ordering, deterministic enums).
4) Security & procurement: While evals run, we’ll share SOC2 evidence and a one-page MSA summary; Marissa will coordinate early commercial terms.

Deliverables (expected)
- Benchmarks_summary_q2.pdf: field-level scores, latency, cost estimate at your throughput.
- prompt_set_v1.json: canonical prompts and expected JSON schema.
- sample mutual action plan: milestones + owners (mutual_action_plan_20260722.xlsx).

Ask from you
- Share a 500-note anonymized sample (S3 link or secure upload) and the canonical schema you want for the JSON output (if different from our attached).
- Confirm whether this needs to run inside Acme VPC or whether a Dedicated instance is acceptable for the eval.

Timing
- If you can share the sample by EOD Thu (23 Jul), we’ll return an initial results pack by Fri 30 Jul.

Thanks — looping Ben and Marissa for engineering & commercial alignment.

—
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model-fit & structured-output eval plan (next steps)

Thanks Soojin — that plan looks good and realistic. A couple of clarifications before we send sample data: 

1) JSON schema validation: how strictly does Redwood enforce schema compliance on function-calling paths? We need to ensure downstream systems do not break if the model produces occasional extra keys or nested arrays. Do you run schema validation + reconcile/repair automatically, or is that an engineering checklist we should manage?

2) Retries/backoff: when using function calling, what is the recommended retry strategy for transient schema validation failures vs. model hallucinations? For example, do you recommend an exponential backoff with n=2 retries, or a more conservative approach, and do you surface retry metadata in logs?

3) Security: we require SOC2 Type II evidence and a statement about data residency for the eval. Can you send the SOC2 report and confirm whether eval data can be retained by Redwood for debugging?

4) Commercial: we’re comfortable with an eval on Dedicated if it simplifies PHI handling. One ask — can you provide a short statement of expected cost for a 2-week Dedicated eval (ballpark) so I can pre-clear with procurement?

If you can answer the above we’ll prepare the anonymized S3 bundle (expects a presigned upload link).

Best,
Priya Shah
Director, Data Science — Acme Health
priya@acmehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Initial engineering notes: schema validation + retry behavior (short)

Priya / Soojin / Marissa — quick tech note after spinning up a small dedicated runner and running 100 sample notes through the attached prompt set: 

Highlights:
- Schema validation: 100 samples -> 87 accepted, 9 repaired (common fixes: missing med_dosage field -> null, medications string -> coerced list), 4 rejected (ambiguous nested lists). We attach 3 sanitized examples of repairs in the drive folder.
- Retry/backoff recommendation: start with 1 immediate attempt (no delay), then up to 2 retries with 700ms and 1200ms delays respectively. Retries improved field-level precision by ~3% on the repaired cohort.
- Fallback policy: for notes longer than 1,500 tokens we recommend routing to the 14b variant to avoid truncation-induced hallucination.
- Logs & observability: we surface retry_count, final_status (accepted/repaired/rejected), and model_variant in Redwood Console tracing. We can add a JSON-LD trace per request if Acme wants more structured audit records.

Next steps I’ll execute if you confirm: run the full 500-note job on Dedicated and produce the final Benchmarks_summary_q2.pdf. If Acme prefers private on-prem run we’ll ship the eval package and a runbook.

Ben Carter
Staff ML Engineer — Redwood Inference
